## What it is

A webcam eye test you can run on your own computer. It shows a chart of classic Snellen
letters, "Tumbling E" shapes or Landolt C rings, sizes them to how far you are from the
screen, and tests each eye in turn.

The demo runs entirely in the browser: the camera stays on your device and no video is
uploaded. It needs a webcam and a bank card (or any card the same size), which is used
as a ruler to measure the screen and calibrate the camera.

## What I built

Rapid deployable eye testing is still stuck in the 20th Century, with most online
Snellen tests requiring a tape measure, a television sized screen, rock-steady seating,
and a second pair of hands.

This project aimed to use a computer vision solution so
lightweight that it could run in-browser, with the added benefit of keeping all patient
data on their own device, so no strict patient confidentiality to worry about.

## How it works

- The same Python package runs on the desktop and in the browser. In the browser,
  [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) runs it with numpy and OpenCV.
- MediaPipe's Face Landmarker tracks the face; a bank card, held to the screen and
  then to the forehead, gives the scale for the screen and the camera.
- Chart sizes come from the same geometry code in all versions, in device pixels,
  and font resizes dynamically as the patients' head changes distance from the screen.
